expected_english: to be; To exist or live; to take place.

with; Preposition indicating accompaniment, tool, or manner.

to bloom / to flourish / to open up; Verb describing a flower opening or a person reaching their full potential and happiness.
to get into debt; Pronominal verb expressing the state of owing money or the process of accumulating debts.
to get rich / to enrich oneself; Pronominal verb expressing the process of becoming wealthy or adding value to oneself/something.
to get poor / to become impoverished; Pronominal verb expressing the process of losing wealth or becoming less fertile/rich in quality.

to be frightened / to take fright; Pronominal verb expressing the act of feeling fear or being startled by something.
to apologize / to excuse oneself; Pronominal verb expressing the act of saying sorry for a mistake or declining an invitation.

to take revenge / to get back at; Pronominal verb expressing the act of settling a score for an offense committed against oneself.
to escape / to slip away / to get out; Pronominal verb meaning to manage to get free from a place or a person's grip.
to host / to lodge / to shelter / to host (website); Verb meaning to provide temporary accommodation for someone or to store a website on a server.
to sink in / to push in / to plunge; Pronominal verb expressing the act of going deep into a soft substance (like mud) or becoming more involved in a situation.

to stabilize / to steady; Verb meaning to make something firm, steady, or unlikely to change suddenly (like prices or a patient's condition).

to skate / to skid (wheel) / to spin one's wheels / to acquire a patina; Verb meaning to move on skates or for wheels to spin on a slippery surface without moving forward. Figuratively: to make no progress.
to strive / to try hard / to endeavor / to exert oneself; Pronominal verb meaning to make a great physical or mental effort to achieve a difficult goal.
to persist doggedly / to strive / to be bent on / to lash out; Pronominal verb meaning to apply oneself to something with extreme energy and persistence, or to attack something/someone repeatedly.
to be stubborn / to persist / to insist / to persevere; Pronominal verb meaning to continue doing something even when others disagree or when it is clear that one is wrong.
to flow away / to elapse (time) / to sell (stock); Pronominal verb describing liquid flowing out, time passing by, or goods being sold off.
to stroll / to loaf / to dawdle / to saunter; Verb describing a slow, relaxed walk for pleasure, looking at things along the way (classic French concept of the flâneur).
to infiltrate / to seep into / to sneak in; Verb meaning to secretly enter a group/country to get information, or for a liquid to pass slowly into a material.
to harvest (grapes) / to destroy (slang) / to waste (slang); Verb specifically meaning to harvest grapes for winemaking, or slang for completely destroying or wasting an opportunity.
to immortalize / to capture (in a photo); Verb meaning to make someone or something live forever in memory, art, or history, or to take a photo of a moment.
to stabilize / to steady / to balance; Verb meaning to make something firm and steady so it does not change or fall, used for physics, health, or the economy.
to obscure / to hide / to mask / to eclipse; Verb meaning to hide something from view or to prevent information from being known, often in a deliberate or systematic way.
to hasten / to be eager / to rush / to lose no time; Pronominal verb meaning to do something quickly and with enthusiasm, often to please someone or to be the first to do it.
to hurry up / to rush / to make haste; Pronominal verb meaning to move or act more quickly than usual, especially when there is a deadline or a delay.
to get busy / to bustle about / to speed things up / to be active; Pronominal verb meaning to start working harder or moving faster to finish a task, or for a process to be accelerated.
to be busy / to bustle about / to be occupied; Pronominal verb meaning to be very busy with many small tasks, often appearing very active and focused.
to be restless / to shake / to wave / to stir / to be turbulent; Pronominal verb meaning to move around nervously, to shake an object, or for a crowd/sea to become turbulent and unstable.
to get annoyed / to get worked up / to lose one's cool / to get nervous; Pronominal verb meaning to become irritated or lose one's patience, often resulting in visible anger or stress.

to get irritated / to become inflamed (skin) / to be annoyed; Pronominal verb meaning to feel a slight but persistent anger, or for a part of the body to become red and painful from rubbing or chemicals.
to get angry / to fall out with someone / to take offense; Pronominal verb meaning to become angry or to stop being friends with someone after a disagreement.
to lose one's temper / to fly into a rage / to be carried away; Pronominal verb meaning to suddenly and violently lose control of one's emotions, or for a horse to bolt out of control.
to be furious / to fume / to be seething / to be mad (informal); Verb meaning to feel an intense, internal anger that makes you want to scream or take action, often without saying much.
to turn greyish / to be gloomy / to drizzle; Verb describing the weather becoming grey and gloomy, or for a landscape to lose its bright colors.
to baptize / to name / to nickname / to water down (wine); Verb meaning to perform the Christian ceremony of baptism, to give a name to a person or an object, or informally to add water to wine.
to personalize / to customize / to personify; Verb meaning to design or change something so that it is exactly what one specific person needs or likes, or to represent an idea as a human being.
to state / to set forth / to enunciate / to articulate; Formal verb meaning to express a law, a principle, or a fact in a very clear and precise way, or to pronounce words clearly.
to inventory / to make an inventory of / to take stock of; Verb meaning to count and list all the goods in a shop, or all the furniture in a house, usually for tax or insurance purposes.

to frame / to structure / to build the framework of / to skeletonize; Verb meaning to build the wooden frame of a house or a ship, or figuratively to give a strong and logical structure to a book or a speech.
to rule / to govern / to manage / to boss around; Slightly pejorative verb meaning to rule a country or a house in a very strict and bossy way, as if you are the only one with power.
to empower / to authorize / to qualify / to entitle; Formal verb meaning to give someone the legal right or the necessary skills to perform a specific task or to sign a document.
to mission / to assign a mission / to send on a task; Verb meaning to give someone a very specific and important goal to reach, often involving a journey or a secret task.
to reward / to recompense / to prize / to compensate; Common verb meaning to give something good to someone because they worked hard, behaved well, or achieved something great.
to devote oneself / to sacrifice oneself / to dedicate oneself; Pronominal verb meaning to give all your time, energy, and love to help another person or to make a project succeed.

to suggest / to influence by suggestion / to hypnotize / to put ideas into someone's head; Verb meaning to use psychological power or repeated words to make someone believe or do something without them realizing it is your idea.

to get along / to reach an agreement / to hear each other / to be understood; Pronominal verb meaning for two people to have a friendly relationship, or for a group to successfully reach a shared decision after a discussion.

to agree / to match / to grant each other / to harmonize; Pronominal verb meaning for colors or ideas to look/sound good together, or for two people to give each other a specific right or a moment of time.

to reconcile / to make up / to become friends again / to harmonize; Pronominal verb meaning to become friends again after a fight or a long period of silence, or to make two opposing ideas work together.

to radiate / to beam / to spread (pain) / to expose to radiation; Verb meaning to send out light or heat in all directions from a center, for a pain to spread from one part of the body to another, or to use rays for medical treatment.

to slip away / to vanish / to eclipse oneself / to fade out; Verb meaning to leave a meeting or a party very discreetly without saying goodbye, or for a celestial body to be hidden.
to evaporate / to vanish / to disappear / to waste away; Verb meaning for a liquid to turn into gas, or figuratively for a person or a sum of money to disappear completely and suddenly.

to vanish into thin air / to volatilize / to disappear suddenly; Verb meaning to turn into a very light gas, or figuratively for a criminal or a physical object to disappear so fast that no trace is left.
to dissipate / to vanish / to clear (fog) / to waste (money/time); Verb meaning for fog, a smell, or an emotion to disappear slowly, or for a student to stop paying attention and waste their energy.
to faint / to vanish / to pass out / to fade away; Verb meaning to lose consciousness for a short time, or figuratively for a sound or a hope to disappear slowly until nothing remains.

to slump / to sag / to go to seed / to become soft / to loll; Verb meaning to lose its shape or firmness (like a cushion or a person's body), or figuratively for someone to lose their energy and willpower and become lazy.

to collapse / to cave in / to break down (crying) / to plummet (prices); Verb meaning for a structure to fall inward, or figuratively for a person to lose all their emotional strength and start crying, or for stock market prices to drop very fast.

to fall down / to crash down / to strike (storm) / to swoop down; Verb meaning to fall down with great force (like a tree or a house), for a storm or a disaster to strike a place, or for a bird of prey to attack suddenly from the sky.

to sink / to plunge / to go deeper / to drive in (a nail); Verb meaning to move further down into a soft material (like mud or a chair), or figuratively to get more involved in a difficult situation or a lie.

to encrust / to embed / to overstay one's welcome / to stick around; Verb meaning for a substance to form a hard layer on a surface (like lime in a pipe), or figuratively for a person to stay in a house or a job where they are no longer wanted.
to interfere / to meddle / to intrude / to intervene (unwanted); Verb meaning to get involved in someone else's private business or a political situation without having the right or being invited.
to interfere / to meddle / to ingest / to swallow; Verb meaning to swallow food or medicine, or figuratively for a country or an organization to meddle in the internal affairs of another.

to insinuate oneself / to creep in / to worm one's way in / to suggest subtly; Verb meaning to enter a place or a group slowly and cleverly, or to suggest an idea indirectly and often with a bad intention.
to slip / to slide / to creep / to steal in; Verb meaning to move smoothly and quietly into a place (like a hand into a glove or a person into a room) without making a noise.
to weave / to slip through / to sneak / to thread one's way; Verb meaning to move through a narrow space or a crowd by changing directions quickly to avoid being stopped or seen.
to nestle / to nest / to hide away / to be perched; Verb meaning for a bird to build a nest, or figuratively for a person or an object to find a small, comfortable, and hidden place to stay.

to blossom / to flourish / to open up / to radiate happiness; Verb meaning for a flower to open its petals, or figuratively for a person to reach their full potential and be completely happy and balanced in life.
to wither / to wilt / to fade / to tarnish (reputation); Verb meaning for a plant to lose its water and freshness, or for a person's skin to lose its beauty, or for a reputation to be damaged.

to contract / to tighten / to shrink / to catch (a disease); Verb meaning for a muscle to become shorter and tighter to produce movement, or for an object to become smaller because of cold, or to catch a virus.

to disintegrate / to fall apart / to break up / to decay (radioactive); Verb meaning to break into small pieces or to be destroyed completely, often used for a rocket entering the atmosphere or for a social structure that no longer holds together.

to clear up / to brighten / to thin out (hair) / to clarify; Verb meaning for the sky to become blue again after rain, or for hair to become less thick, or for a mystery to be explained and understood.

to be situated / to be located / to lie / to find oneself; Verb meaning to be in a specific place or to have a specific position in a hierarchy or a period of time.
to be found / to be located / to be / to find oneself; Very common verb meaning to be in a particular place, or to be in a particular state or situation (like feeling tired).

to introduce oneself / to present oneself / to appear / to arise; Verb meaning to tell someone your name, or to go to an office or a court for an interview or a trial, or for an opportunity to happen.
to introduce oneself / to get in / to enter / to insert oneself; Verb meaning to enter a place, sometimes without permission, or to put yourself into a group or a conversation.
